#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Records the real-app demo (see README.md in this folder). Needs: Xvfb, PulseAudio, ffmpeg, the Pawse
# backend running with GEMINI_API_KEY and GRADIUM_API_KEY, and the React app built (cd web && npm run build).
set -euo pipefail
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
cd "$HERE/.."
APP_URL="${APP_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:8765/app/?live=1}"
OWNER_WAV="${OWNER_WAV:-$HERE/owner-line.wav}"
NARRATION_WAV="${NARRATION_WAV-$HERE/narrator-intro.wav}"  # narrator over the opening; NARRATION_WAV= (empty) to skip
[ -f "$NARRATION_WAV" ] || NARRATION_WAV=""
MIMI_DIR="${MIMI_DIR:-/mnt/pawse-demo-out/mimi}"  # make-mimi-clip.py output; skipped when missing
OUT_DIR="${OUT_DIR:-/mnt/pawse-demo-out}"  # heavy media stays off the repo disk
mkdir -p "$OUT_DIR"

# Audio: Chromium plays into the null sink "rec" (ffmpeg records its monitor); the owner's line is
# played into the null sink "mic", exposed to Chromium as the source "owner_mic".
pulseaudio --check 2>/dev/null || pulseaudio --start --exit-idle-time=-1
pactl list short sinks | grep -q '\brec\b' || pactl load-module module-null-sink sink_name=rec sink_properties=device.description=rec >/dev/null
pactl list short sinks | grep -q '\bmic\b' || pactl load-module module-null-sink sink_name=mic sink_properties=device.description=mic >/dev/null
pactl list short sources | grep -q owner_mic || pactl load-module module-remap-source master=mic.monitor source_name=owner_mic >/dev/null
pactl set-default-sink rec
pactl set-default-source owner_mic

# The stage page and the opening clip, served together.
STAGE_DIR="$(mktemp -d)"
ln -s "$HERE/stage.html" "$STAGE_DIR/stage.html"
MIMI_ENV=()
if [ -f "$MIMI_DIR/mimi-16x9.mp4" ]; then
  ln -s "$MIMI_DIR/mimi-16x9.mp4" "$STAGE_DIR/mimi.mp4"
  MIMI_ENV=(MIMI_INTRO=1 MIMI_CAMERA="$MIMI_DIR/mimi-9x16.mp4" MIMI_STILL="$MIMI_DIR/mimi-still.jpg")
fi
python3 -m http.server 4180 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory "$STAGE_DIR" >/dev/null 2>&1 &
STAGE_PID=$!
trap 'kill $STAGE_PID 2>/dev/null || true; rm -rf "$STAGE_DIR"' EXIT
sleep 1

RAW="$OUT_DIR/pawse-demo-real.mkv"
STAGE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:4180/stage.html?app=$(python3 -c 'import sys,urllib.parse;print(urllib.parse.quote(sys.argv[1]))' "$APP_URL")" \
env "${MIMI_ENV[@]}" OWNER_WAV="$OWNER_WAV" NARRATION_WAV="$NARRATION_WAV" OUT="$RAW" \
  xvfb-run -a -s "-screen 0 1920x1080x24" node "$HERE/record-real.mjs"

# Deliverable: silent waits shortened to fit 2:00, h264 + loudness-normalised AAC mp4. Capped at 4 GB RAM so a
# memory regression in the cut fails fast instead of freezing the machine.
CUT=(python3 "$HERE/make-cut.py" "$RAW" "$OUT_DIR/pawse-demo-real.mp4" "${TARGET_SECONDS:-120}")
if systemd-run --user --scope -q -p MemoryMax=4G true 2>/dev/null; then
  systemd-run --user --scope -q -p MemoryMax=4G "${CUT[@]}"
else
  "${CUT[@]}"

content.text: Now the check script. It counts how often the owner's line occurs in the raw take using the same cross-correlation that found the bug:

input.content:
"""Fail a take whose owner's line is heard more (or less) than once.

check-owner-line.py <raw.mkv> <owner-line.wav>

The recorder plays the owner's line once. A second copy means foreign audio reached the recording (another take or an
audio test playing into the same PulseAudio), which repeats "Hi Pawse, my cat Mimi is limping" over the video.
Each 1.5 s slice of the line is found by normalised cross-correlation (8 kHz mono); a play counts when its start is
matched by the slice that opens the line.
"""
import subprocess
import sys

import numpy as np

RATE, SLICE, MATCH = 8000, 1.5, 0.45


def pcm(path):
    out = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-i", path, "-ac", "1", "-ar", str(RATE), "-f", "s16le", "-"],
                         capture_output=True, check=True).stdout
    return np.frombuffer(out, np.int16).astype(np.float32)


def starts(x, tpl):
    """Times (s) where tpl occurs in x."""
    t = tpl - tpl.mean()
    t /= np.linalg.norm(t)
    n, size = len(t), len(x) + len(t)
    c = np.fft.irfft(np.fft.rfft(x, size) * np.fft.rfft(t[::-1], size))[n - 1:len(x)]
    energy = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(x.astype(np.float64) ** 2)])
    e = np.sqrt(energy[n:] - energy[:-n])[:len(c)]
    nc = np.where(e > 3000, c[:len(e)] / np.maximum(e, 1), 0)  # silence would divide by ~0
    peaks = []
    for i in np.flatnonzero(nc > MATCH):
        if not peaks or i - peaks[-1][0] > RATE // 2:
            peaks.append([i, nc[i]])
        elif nc[i] > peaks[-1][1]:
            peaks[-1] = [i, nc[i]]
    return [i / RATE for i, _ in peaks]


raw, owner = pcm(sys.argv[1]), pcm(sys.argv[2])
plays = starts(raw, owner[:int(SLICE * RATE)])
print(f"owner's line heard {len(plays)}x at {', '.join(f'{t:.1f}s' for t in plays) or '-'} in {sys.argv[1]}")
if len(plays) != 1:
    sys.exit("Foreign or missing owner audio: record again, with nothing else playing into this take's PulseAudio.")

# Real-app demo recording

Records the 2-minute Mimi demo from the **real app** (`/app/?live=1`), not the mock in `../mock/`. One command,
one uncut take, with the sound the app actually played.

| Beat | What runs | Live or simulated |
|---|---|---|
| Owner says "my cat Mimi is limping" | Gemini Live hears the line through a virtual microphone and answers out loud | Live (the owner's line is a pre-generated Gemini TTS clip, `owner-line.wav`) |
| Triage card | Gemini Live calls the care tool, the backend runs Gemini care triage | Live |
| Nearby clinics | Backend clinic search around Zurich | Live (Gemini Maps grounding, needs `GEMINI_API_KEY`) |
| German vet script | Gemini drafts the German script with English subtitles | Live |
| Vet and insurer calls | The app's phone rehearsal: Pawse's German lines spoken by Gradium | Gradium voice live, the vet's and insurer's replies simulated and labelled so on screen. Nothing is dialled |
| Summary | Plan page built from the steps above | Live UI over the simulated call results |

The stage around the phone shows a caption per beat and `LIVE` / `SIMULATED` badges, so nothing simulated is
presented as real.

## Run

Needs Linux with Xvfb, PulseAudio (`sudo apt-get install pulseaudio pulseaudio-utils xvfb`), ffmpeg, Node 20+,
`npm install` in `demo/`, the app built (`cd web && npm run build`) and the backend running with `GEMINI_API_KEY`
and `GRADIUM_API_KEY` in `.env`:

```sh
uvicorn pawse.app:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8765 &
bash demo/real/record-real.sh          # APP_URL=... to point at another server
```

Output in `/mnt/pawse-demo-out/` (`OUT_DIR=` to change): `pawse-demo-real.mp4` (deliverable, silent waits shortened to fit 2:00 by `make-cut.py`; speech is never cut), the raw `.mkv`, and `-marks.json` (when each
caption appeared). A failed beat stops the take and saves `-fail.png`.

To change the owner's spoken line: `python demo/real/make-owner-line.py "<text>" demo/real/owner-line.wav`
(Gemini TTS, reads `GEMINI_API_KEY` from `.env`).

The opening has a narrator (`narrator-intro.wav`, Gemini TTS voice Charon, about 12 s) played into `rec` only, so
Gemini Live never hears it; the clip's own sound drops under it and the app starts only after it ends. Skip it with
`NARRATION_WAV= bash demo/real/record-real.sh`. To change it: `python demo/real/make-owner-line.py "<text>"
demo/real/narrator-intro.wav Charon` (write Pawse as "Pause" so TTS says it right).

## How the sound gets in

PulseAudio gets two null sinks. Chromium plays into `rec`, and ffmpeg records `rec.monitor` together with the X
screen, so picture and sound share one clock. The owner's line is played into `mic`, which Chromium sees as the
microphone `owner_mic`, and also into `rec` so viewers hear it. Every take differs a little: Gemini's wording and
timing are live.
